newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba-extent of forex revaluation not decided yet.
newsitem.headline: Buba-extent of forex revaluation not decided yet.

text.p: Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer and Finance Minister Theo Waigel did not decide in their meeting on Thursday on the level at which currency reserves held at the bank will be valued, the bank said.

Speaking in response to media reports that the revaluation of the currency reserves would lead to a transfer of up to 15 billion marks to the Bonn government, a spokesman for the central bank said: "No figures on the outcome of a revaluation were decided on, nor is it possible at present to define a figure."
Earlier, German government coalition sources said that Waigel and Tietmeyer agreed the Bundesbank would in future assess its dollar reserves using an exchange rate of at least 1.50 marks.
Waigel and Tietmeyer said on Thursday they had reached an agreement on revaluing the central bank's currency reserves.

The Bundesbank will use room provided by the Maastricht Treaty to revalue its foreign exchange reserves in 1997 using accounting rules provided for in existing law, the bank and the finance ministry said in a joint statement.
"These make it possible to carry out a valuation close to market prices and retain the principle of lowest value," the statement said.
The Bundesbank is believed to hold $65 billion in reserves. Its currency reserves consist entirely of dollars.
